hero.title: Handwritten Digits
hero.subtitle: 784 pixels, ten classes.
hero.tagline: A Keras notebook that loads MNIST, flattens each 28×28 digit, and trains a small dense network to ten classes.
hero.impact: No camera and no saved model file. The notebook trains, scores train and test, and prints predictions for the first 100 test images next to their labels.

problems.d: MNIST arrives as 28×28 arrays. The notebook divides by 255, then reshapes train to 60000×784 and test to 10000×784.
keras.utils.to_categorical turns the digit id into a one-hot row so the loss can be categorical crossentropy.
No convolutions. Three ReLU hidden layers, then a 10-way softmax.
After fit, evaluate runs on train and on test. argmax on the first 100 predictions is printed beside argmax of the one-hot labels.

layers.title: MNIST
layers.desc: tensorflow.keras.datasets.mnist.load_data(). One sample is shown with imshow before scaling

layers.title: Scale and flatten
layers.desc: Divide by 255. Reshape to 784. One-hot the labels. Labels stay unscaled

layers.title: Sequential
layers.desc: Dense 512 ReLU, dense 64 ReLU, dense 32 ReLU, dense 10 softmax. Adam and categorical crossentropy

layers.title: Evaluate
layers.desc: 100 epochs, then evaluate on train and test, then predict the first 100 test rows

highlights: Train and test evaluate, plus a 100-row prediction check
